audit.whatIsWrong: Both chart layers read Aurora/Skill/Olaf/Olaf/Aurora/Olaf/Olaf while the packet levelChart reads Skill/Aurora/Aurora/Aurora/Aurora/Aurora/Olaf — and every why[] from 1 to 5 describes Aurora winning that stage.
audit.why: whys[1] 'every time I throw an axe to engage she just E-blinks the gap', whys[2] 'chip me down faster than I can close', whys[3] 'I bleed health', whys[5] 'the poke-and-blink pattern is at its strongest' — five Aurora rows, three of them marked Olaf. Row 0 was marked Aurora while its own why claimed Olaf wins first contact; the packet says Skill and the prose is now written to match.
audit.corrected: Chart set to Skill, Aurora, Aurora, Aurora, Aurora, Aurora, Olaf in BOTH layers as one atomic group, with ratings re-scaled.

audit.whatIsWrong: The level-6 spike was written as Olaf's, on the premise that Ragnarok cleanses Aurora's CC. It is her spike per the packet, and Ragnarok does not do that job here.
audit.why: Ragnarok (100/90/80s) grants armour, MR and immunity to disables while attacking. Aurora's crowd control is slows only — The Weirding (E) 'damages and slows enemies before Aurora hops backward'; Between Worlds (R, 140/120/100s) 'damages and slows any enemies it hits' then leaves a slowing area she can teleport across. Immunity to disables does not answer slows, so at 6 the ult buys resists and survivability, not freedom.
audit.corrected: Level 6 handed to Aurora; Ragnarok restated as resists plus a run-down rather than a cleanse.

audit.whatIsWrong: FABRICATED CC AND WRONG SLOTS. 'Her root' appears in whys[2], whys[4], early, mid, late, wants.you[1], wants.foe[0] and wants.foe[2]; Aurora has no root anywhere. 'W exile' is also invented — Across the Veil (W, 22/21/20/19/18s) is a leap that turns her invisible with bonus Move Speed, not an exile applied to you.
audit.why: Riot text per slot: P Spirit Abjuration heals her off exorcised spirits; Q Twofold Hex (9/8.5/8/7.5/7s) curses on the way out and is recast to drag the curses back through you; W Across the Veil is her leap plus invisibility; E The Weirding (15/14/13/12/11s) is a slow with a backward hop; R Between Worlds is a leap, shockwave slow and a traversable slowing zone. No root, no exile, no silence.
audit.corrected: Every root reference replaced with the real ability and effect; the recast half of Twofold Hex — the part that actually catches you when you chase — stated in early.

audit.whatIsWrong: 'Vicious Strikes (W) omnivamp' in spikes[2] and wants.you[2], plus 'W omnivamp' in whys[2] and mid. Vicious Strikes is a retired name; the current W is Tough It Out — attack speed plus a shield, 16/15/14/13/12s, no healing.
audit.why: Riot text, Olaf W: 'Olaf's Attack Speed is increased and he gains a Shield.' His lifesteal is Berserker Rage (P), scaling with missing health.
audit.corrected: Renamed and restated as a shield in all four.

edits.before: Axe-slow + W sustain wins the first trades. Identify how Aurora contests the first waves before you commit anything.
edits.after: Undertow's slow can land before she hops away with The Weirding, but she can equally just walk back — level 1 is close.

edits.before: Full kit online — your core pattern starts now. Keep the wave near your side so Aurora must walk into your engage range.
edits.after: Her Q poke and The Weirding's hop refuse the melee trade — from 3 you cannot close without baiting the 15s E first.

edits.before: The lane-control window: trade around Twofold Hex's cooldown and bank small leads. If ahead, freeze and deny; if behind, farm safe.
edits.after: She keeps hopping your engage and re-poking through 4-5, so you bleed health without ever landing the stick your all-in needs.

edits.before: Ragnarok deletes CC — once you press R, nothing he has stops the run-down. Reassess every all-in at 6 — Aurora's ultimate changes the math too.
edits.after: Ragnarok is resists, not a cleanse — Aurora's crowd control is slows. At 6 Between Worlds repositions her clean out of your 400-range run-down.

edits.before: Sundered Sky is your spike — force fights the moment it completes, on Twofold Hex's cooldown.
edits.after: Her first item makes the poke-and-hop pattern strongest — she works you from outside Q range.

edits.before: My level-1 Undertow slow lands before she can angle her E blink, so I win first contact and get a free auto with my passive ramping.
edits.after: My level-1 Undertow slow can land before she hops with The Weirding, but she can also just step back — first contact is a coinflip here.

edits.before: Her root plus Q poke chip me down faster than I can close, and my W omnivamp does nothing while she refuses the melee trade.
edits.after: Twofold Hex's recast and The Weirding's slow chip me faster than I can close, and my W shield does nothing at range.

edits.before: She gets her level-6 combo online too, and if I burn Ragnarok early she roots and W-exiles me the moment it expires.
edits.after: Her 6 arrives too: Between Worlds slows and repositions her, and Across the Veil takes her invisible out of my reach.

edits.before: Ragnarok (R) cleanses her root and ignores her W exile, so once she blows that combo you can run her down through CC immunity.
edits.after: Ragnarok gives resists and disable-immunity, but Aurora's crowd control is slows — it frees nothing. Its value is surviving her burst.

edits.after: With Bramble/Cleaver and Tough It Out's shield you absorb her Q poke in a sustained trade, but only if you caught The Weirding's 15s down.

edits.after: Hold Ragnarok for after she commits The Weirding's hop, then dive while she has no second escape ready

edits.after: Force the melee all-in at 1st item where Tough It Out's shield absorbs her poke

edits.after: Poke you with Twofold Hex's out-and-back curse and never let you close the gap

edits.after: Bait your Ragnarok early, then Across the Veil out of range and burst you once it drops

edits.before: Level 1 is genuinely mine if I lead with a tip-range Undertow — the axe slow sticks her before she can read it and E-blink, and I walk up for a free auto with my passive already ticking. But the second she hits 2 and 3 this flips: she Q-pokes my health bar and the instant I throw a Q to engage, she E-blinks the gap and I've spent my slow on air. Don't chase her into her own minions for a refunded axe — that's where her root lands and the poke adds up. Farm, hold Q for when she's committed forward, and accept I'm behind on the health bar here.
edits.after: Level 1 is close if I lead with a tip-range Undertow — the axe slow can stick her before she reads it and hops with The Weirding, and I walk up for a free auto with my passive already ticking. But the second she hits 2 and 3 it flips: Twofold Hex curses on the way out and is recast to drag back through me, and the instant I throw a Q she hops the gap and I've spent the slow on air. Don't chase into her minions for a refunded axe — that is where the recast lands and the poke adds up. Farm, hold Q for when she commits forward.

edits.before: Levels 4-6 she still edges me because my whole kit wants a melee all-in and her E blink plus root keep refusing it. The mistake is ulting on cooldown — Ragnarok cleanses her root and makes her CC useless, but if I pop it and she just E-blinks away, I've wasted my one answer and she roots me when it drops. Bait the blink first: walk in like I'm committing, make her burn E, THEN Q-slow and R-dive while she has no second escape. My W omnivamp only matters if I actually land hits, so the whole lane is forcing one clean stick.
edits.after: Levels 4-6 she edges me because my whole kit wants a melee all-in and The Weirding's slow-and-hop keeps refusing it. The mistake is expecting Ragnarok to fix that — her crowd control is slows, not disables, so the immunity frees nothing; what it buys is armour, MR and an uninterrupted run-down. Bait the hop first: walk in like I'm committing, make her burn the 15s E, THEN Q-slow and R-dive while she has no second escape. Tough It Out only matters if I land hits, so the lane is one clean stick.

edits.before: This is the one window that's mine. Aurora is a squishy skirmish-mage, and once I have a couple of bruiser items my E true damage and Ragnarok let me ignore her root and delete her in the dive — she can't kite an unstoppable Olaf the way a real ranged hypercarry can. I have to convert here, though: I'm not a true scaler, so I want to be ending the game on her, not waiting. Catch her sided, R through whatever she throws, and the omnivamp from W keeps me topped through her burst.
edits.after: This is the one window that's mine. Aurora is a squishy skirmish-mage, and once I have a couple of bruiser items Reckless Swing's true damage cuts her whatever she builds and Ragnarok's armour and MR carry me through the burst — she can't kite me the way a real ranged hypercarry can. I have to convert here, though: I'm not a true scaler, so I want to be ending the game on her, not waiting. Catch her sided and let Tough It Out's shield cover the poke as I close.

notes: WIN RATE CONFLICT carried over from the mirror and NOT edited: the aurora packet reports 64.86% over 74 games while this olaf packet reports 51.35% over 777 games, implying roughly 48.65% for Aurora. The 777-game sample is the trustworthy one; the aurora-side diffRating was already set to 5/10 for this reason. Aurora's R carries a derived 'hardCC' flag that Riot's description does not support (shockwave damage and slow, then a slowing zone) — no stun or root claim was made anywhere in this slice, and that is why the Ragnarok-cleanse premise had to go.
